Problem Statement:
Jack becomes adventurous suddenly and decides to play the game of "array" jumping .In this game he will be given an arrray A of N integers. When Jack is at a position i in the Array A (1<=i<=N , we use 1-based indexing here) , he can jump to any position A[i] - this is counted as one jump.Find the minimum number of moves that is required for Jack to reach the end of the array- index N from the index 1. 
Input Description:
The first line contains a single integer N denoting the number of positions in the arrayThe next line contains N integers as described in the problem statement 
Output Description:
Output a single integer : the minimum number of jumps required to reach the end of the array 
Sample Input:
10
3 3 10 10 6 3 4 4 1 7 
Sample Output:
2 
Explanation:
The jumps are : 1(3)->4(10)->10(7) which is the end of array (1-based indexing) . So only 2 jumps are required.
